title: Can yesterday reduce the noise?
hook: Use a pre-score to adjust outcomes, then inspect the remaining spread.

knows: arithmetic means, rates and simple plotted values
doesNotKnow: adjust for each user's pre-experiment behavior and confidence intervals narrow.

misconception: Treating cuped as valid without checking the stated model, denominators or causal assumptions.
objective: adjust for each user's pre-experiment behavior and confidence intervals narrow.
keyState: Both finite cases completed; their computed summaries retained.

claims.text: For pre-score X=1,2,3,4 and post-score Y=3,3,5,5, use θ=cov(X,Y)/var(X)=.8 and Yadj=Y−θ(X−mean X). What variance remains?
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-cuped/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Pre score X=[1,2,3,4], post Y=[3,3,5,5]. Xvariance1.25,Yvariance1,cov1, optimaltheta.8. AdjustedY=[4.2,3.4,4.6,3.8] variance.2; reduction80%.

claims.text: The adjusted outcome retains variance 0.2; the unadjusted outcome retains 1. The pre-score predicts variation that can be removed without shifting this sample’s mean of 4.
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-cuped/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Pre score X=[1,2,3,4], post Y=[3,3,5,5]. Xvariance1.25,Yvariance1,cov1, optimaltheta.8. AdjustedY=[4.2,3.4,4.6,3.8] variance.2; reduction80%.

claims.text: CUPED uses a pre-treatment covariate rather than a treatment consequence. This exact toy calculation illustrates variance reduction; real uncertainty estimates must respect how the adjustment coefficient and experiment were estimated.
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-cuped/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Pre score X=[1,2,3,4], post Y=[3,3,5,5]. Xvariance1.25,Yvariance1,cov1, optimaltheta.8. AdjustedY=[4.2,3.4,4.6,3.8] variance.2; reduction80%.

claims.text: Why should an experiment covariate used for variance reduction be pre-treatment? A post-treatment variable may lie on a causal pathway and change the estimand or introduce bias.
